question: Each normal range covers the middle 95% of healthy people. Across 20 independent tests, what percentage chance has a healthy person of at least one abnormal result?
move: Run enough checks on anything and something will look wrong.
trap: Guessing 5%, the rate for one test, for the whole panel.
hint: Work out the chance that every result lands inside its range, then subtract.
steps: Chance one test comes back normal: 0.95.
Chance at least one is flagged: 1 - 0.358 = 0.642.
reference: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute, EP28-A3c: Defining, Establishing, and Verifying Reference Intervals in the Clinical Laboratory, 2008
